headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error: AutoGPT can read/write files and use shell, while pathway is a non-interactive document processor with no write or network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, so it can ingest untrusted content and act on it. pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file I/O surfaces, so direct bridging is limited, but AutoGPT’s file-based workflows still create an injection path if pathway-produced documents are later consumed as instructions. The pairwise interaction is only indirectly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads pathway-generated files as prompts or task instructions, injection becomes active.
IF an operator manually copies pathway output into AutoGPT, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Separate input and instruction directories for AutoGPT.
Prefix pathway outputs with a fixed schema and reject free-form directives.
Disable AutoGPT access to untrusted folders.
Review any file AutoGPT opens before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between pathway outputs and AutoGPT inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has allowlisted network egress and filesystem access, but pathway exposes no file read/write, clipboard, or API calls, so there is no clear shared data path. Because both profiles touch no sensitive data classes and pathway is effectively isolated, leakage risk is limited unless an operator manually moves files between them.
conditions: IF an operator places sensitive files into AutoGPT’s workspace, AutoGPT may transmit them over allowlisted egress.
IF pathway is connected to a shared folder outside the profile, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of AutoGPT’s workspace.
Restrict AutoGPT allowlist to required domains only.
Run pathway on a separate host or container.
Audit any manual file transfers between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while pathway cannot write files, modify git state, or use subprocesses. That makes overlapping mutable-resource conflict unlikely; the main risk is AutoGPT colliding with external files, not with pathway. No shared write surface is documented, so this stays low.
conditions: IF pathway is wrapped by an external orchestrator that writes into AutoGPT’s workspace, file collisions can occur.
IF AutoGPT is pointed at a shared directory, it may overwrite unrelated files.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount AutoGPT workspaces read-only where possible.
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents.
Schedule runs so only one agent writes to a given path.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate actions from file and shell outputs, so if pathway-produced documents are treated as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream actions. pathway itself is a document-processing system with no direct action-taking authority, so the chain is indirect rather than high severity. The lack of documented verification between them keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT consumes pathway output without a verification step, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF AutoGPT is allowed to execute shell actions based on pathway summaries, downstream mistakes can become operational.
mitigations: Require human review before AutoGPT acts on pathway output.
Add a validation step that checks pathway outputs against source data.
Limit AutoGPT to draft-only mode for pathway-derived tasks.
Log and diff all pathway-to-AutoGPT handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on pathway outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched and no secrets or OAuth scopes. With no compliance-sensitive flow identified, there is no specific pairwise compliance breach to score.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, a new compliance review is required.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Record retention settings for both agents.
Verify residency requirements for any regulated workload.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
